newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian railmen halt all but army trains.
newsitem.headline: Croatian railmen halt all but army trains.

text.p: Striking Croatian railway workers extended their stoppage on Tuesday in defiance of pressure by the state railway (HZ) for a return to work.
Strike leader Zlatko Pavletic said only trains carrying supplies for the Croatian army and NATO peacekeepers in neighbouring Bosnia were still running.

Eighty percent of Croatian rail traffic was halted on November 28 when 11,000 HZ employees began a national strike for wage increases and better working conditions. They maintained only a legally required minimum of trains.
Pavletic said the strikers decided to suspend all non-military traffic after HZ sacked a railman who refused to return to work on Monday.
The railway company has denied threatening to sack workers who refused to sign written statements criticising the strike.
"We shall resume the minimum services only after our colleague is back at work," Pavletic told Reuters at Zagreb's deserted main railway station.
HZ said it was losing an estimated 1.6 million kuna (about $300,000) a day due to the stoppage and risked being unable to pay wages for November.
Pavletic said he expected talks with HZ to resume on Tuesday when "we expect the management to realise they acted illegaly and to reinstate our colleague."
He said the strikers were supported by the International Traffic Federation, whose representatives were due in Zagreb on Wednesday.
The government, faced with a wave of unrest, refused to give in to the strikers' demands and said there was no money to increase pay this year.
